nodes.label: Partial alert availability
nodes.rationale: Unavailable alert kinds produce a persistent job warning without failing unrelated sync scopes.

nodes.label: Security alert access
nodes.rationale: Access requires system administration or global Manager plus repository Manager membership.

nodes.label: Security alert tracking
nodes.rationale: Read-only dependency, code, and secret alerts normalize supported GitHub and GitLab data.

nodes.label: Stale active run reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Refresh every locally queued or running run during the next repository sync to correct stale states.

nodes.label: PWA branding cache isolation
nodes.rationale: The service worker does not precache branding configuration or cache protected API data.

nodes.label: Safe normalized alert data
nodes.rationale: Secret values and raw provider payloads must never be stored, logged, or returned.

nodes.label: Silent alert baselines
nodes.rationale: The first successful sync establishes a baseline; later discoveries and transitions may notify.

nodes.label: Incremental listing reuse
nodes.rationale: Reuse runs from provider listings to avoid duplicate requests.

nodes.label: Missing run unknown status
nodes.rationale: A missing provider run becomes UNKNOWN and loses approval state; linked pull-request aggregates refresh.

nodes.label: Provider authoritative state
nodes.rationale: Do not infer completion from age or duplicate names; preserve completedAt when no reliable time exists.

nodes.label: Declaration documentation coverage
nodes.rationale: Checkers verify coverage and nonempty tags; implementation review must still assess documentation accuracy.

nodes.label: Verification commands
nodes.rationale: Formatting, documentation, lint, typecheck, unit tests, and browser checks verify affected work.

nodes.label: Coding guidelines
nodes.rationale: Executable standards cover handwritten code, schemas, tests, scripts, and configuration.

nodes.label: Canonical Vue formatting
nodes.rationale: Prettier and Vue rules preserve significant whitespace and compiled render behavior; two passes must be stable.

nodes.label: Font redistribution conditions
nodes.rationale: Bundled fonts retain copyright and license; font software may not be sold by itself.

nodes.label: Inter font license
nodes.rationale: Inter font software is distributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

nodes.label: Latest release security support
nodes.rationale: Historical documentation does not promise continuing security support for older versions.

nodes.label: Private vulnerability reporting
nodes.rationale: Coordinated private disclosure avoids exposing credentials, customer data, or exploit details.

nodes.label: Bruno API collection
nodes.rationale: Version-controlled requests support manual API checks.

nodes.label: Persisted provider health
nodes.rationale: The health request verifies API and database health and persisted provider sync state.

nodes.label: Domain split Prisma schemas
nodes.rationale: One kebab-case schema file per model or enum keeps definitions organized by domain.

nodes.label: Resource identity and timestamps
nodes.rationale: UUID identity and UTC record timestamps remain distinct from provider event timestamps.

nodes.label: Prototype key rejection
nodes.rationale: Replacement merge semantics reject prototype-control keys from both inputs.

nodes.label: Versioned operations handbook
nodes.rationale: Readers select documentation matching the installed release.

nodes.label: Restricted release promotion
nodes.rationale: Release promotion requires a dedicated restricted GitHub App and remains disabled until configured.

nodes.label: Runtime theming and branding
nodes.rationale: Environment variables and read-only mounts allow installation branding without rebuilding images.

nodes.label: Validated branding endpoints
nodes.rationale: Public branding endpoints expose validated values and explicitly configured assets with no-store caching.

nodes.label: Changesets releases
nodes.rationale: One application version produces matching API and web images after the release pull request merges.

nodes.label: Encrypted provider credentials
nodes.rationale: Provider and notification credentials are encrypted in PostgreSQL rather than stored as environment variables.

nodes.label: Repovio dashboard
nodes.rationale: Read-only workflow, issue, and pull-request dashboard for GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, and Gitea.

nodes.label: Shared Zod contracts
nodes.rationale: Shared contracts avoid deriving API models from untyped responses; DTOs remain thin metadata bridges.

nodes.label: Dependency security maintenance
nodes.rationale: Bounded overrides address glob and minimatch advisories without replacing unaffected API lines.

nodes.label: Documentation index
nodes.rationale: Operations documentation lives in repovio/docs while source-specific maintenance records stay in this repository.

nodes.label: GitHub security setup record
nodes.rationale: Records security settings inspected on November 5, 2026 rather than proof of remote workflow execution.

nodes.label: Bruno secret variables
nodes.rationale: Username, password, and bearer token remain secret variables instead of committed request data.

nodes.label: Generated Prisma client
nodes.rationale: Regenerate the client after schema changes instead of editing generated output.

nodes.label: Clean lockfile verification
nodes.rationale: Existing node_modules does not prove reproducibility; validate a frozen clean install and affected builds.

nodes.label: Deepmerge dependency removal
nodes.rationale: No fixed deepmerge release exists; version-specific patches replace it with @fastify/deepmerge.

nodes.label: Private CodeQL feature gate
nodes.rationale: Private CodeQL runs only when enabled and supported by the existing plan; paid features are not activated automatically.

nodes.label: Mounted branding assets
nodes.rationale: Private file overrides take precedence and stay out of public responses; invalid or oversized assets prevent startup.

nodes.label: Offline OpenAPI export
nodes.rationale: Deterministic contract export avoids production listeners, databases, schedulers, and provider requests.
